title: ff_sws_alphablendaway averages the alpha row below the plane's last on a subsampled odd size
object: the alpha plane of a YUVA420P frame, one of four planes av_frame_get_buffer carves from a single AVBuffer
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the frame is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: a vertical average reads one row past the alpha plane, inside the frame's single AVBuffer
allocator_layer: av_frame_get_buffer over av_malloc: every plane of the frame is carved from ONE AVBuffer, which is what makes the crossing nested
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. The frame, its planes and its single AVBuffer come from real libavutil; the case asserts both structural facts rather than assuming them -- buf[1] == NULL, and a whole row past the alpha plane still inside the buffer (measured slack 1024 bytes). The consumer is reduced to the one average the fix changed, at x = 0 on the last subsampled row, with the fix's own condition subsample_row = y_subsample && (y << y_subsample) + 1 < lum_h as the only difference between the arms. The horizontal half of the same overread, a[2x + 1] past the row's width, is left out; PROVENANCE.md says so.
live_proof: the fix is an ancestor of n9.0.1 (git merge-base --is-ancestor b7946098b1 n9.0.1 succeeds), and the pin carries the fixed form: 'subsample_row' occurs 5 times in n9.0.1:libswscale/alphablend.c while the pre-fix 'x_subsample || y_subsample' condition occurs 0 times, with ff_sws_alphablendaway present as the positive control that the search reaches the file. The case reconstructs the pre-fix consumer shape against the shipped allocator -- the convention at ../../memcached/allocator-repros/README.md:132-135, carried by 27 of the 33 cases in this tree.
distinguishing: the arms differ by the fix's own condition and by nothing else. The frame, the plane, the row and the x index are identical in both; only whether the row below is averaged changes.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm reports crossed=1 contained=1 damage=1, the fixed arm crossed=0 contained=1 damage=0. contained=1 on BOTH arms is the structural claim: a whole row past the plane is inside the frame's one AVBuffer, with 1024 bytes to spare. spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **NOT CAUGHT; the defect reproduced**: the sequence completed with the crossing made, which the case's own CHECKs place inside ONE allocation, so an allocation-granular bound is in bounds for it. The read at offset 160 of the alpha plane lies inside upstream's own 1024-byte padded plane, inside that bound.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. sublet.prediction: PREDICTED: the sequence completes, for the spatial arm's reason plus its own -- revocation has nothing to fire on while the frame is alive. RETRACTED 2026-10-06: this oracle previously said a discriminating reading needs a plane-narrowing adapter. Measured, it does not help: av_frame_get_buffer pads to FFALIGN(height,32), so the alpha plane's OWN allocated extent is 1024 bytes while the logical plane is 160, and this case reads at offset 160 -- inside upstream's own plane extent. An adapter narrowing to FFmpeg's layout cannot see it; only a bound tighter than upstream's own allocation could, and that would fault legitimate code (SIMD tail reads, av_image_copy_to_buffer over padded_height). NOT MEASURED, and not a gap.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08 on this host, revocation ON: the sequence COMPLETES on both arms and prints its own verdict -- VERDICT FIXED on the fixed arm, VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED on the buggy one. **NOT CAUGHT, which CONFIRMS this arm's committed prediction** (the sibling plain-heap corpus's bundle records a REFUTED prediction; this one is the other way round). THE MECHANISM IS THIS CORPUS'S OWN MEASUREMENT, not an inference: av_frame_get_buffer carves every plane from ONE AVBuffer and pads to FFALIGN(height, 32), so the alpha plane's allocated extent is 1024 bytes against a logical 160 -- the row past the plane is still inside the allocation. CheriBSD bounds the allocation, not the plane, so no fault is possible and none occurred. That is the nested-spatial cell stated as a measurement rather than as a prediction: a per-allocation bound is blind here by construction. Platform controls fired in the same boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1`, cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY and SIGPROT.
cheribsd-revocation.note: Measured at last. The earlier note said UNMEASURABLE ON THIS HOST, 'same check as the PoisonCap arms' -- that was true of PoisonCap and WRONG of CheriBSD once a purecap vehicle existed here. The real blocker was specific to this corpus and is now removed: the cases link REAL libavutil, so a purecap libavutil had to be cross-built (verified by ELF flags EF_RISCV_CAP_MODE/EF_RISCV_CHERIABI, not by the build command), and the read probe had to stop being `static` in corpus.h so supervise could resolve it. PoisonCap remains genuinely absent from this host: not yet done is not the same as cannot be done.
